alyssa (eng-runtime): heads-up: seeing a ~2.4x latency regression on Mixtral-7B when serving typical chat traffic since yesterday's runtime push. perf snapshot attached below.
sam (eng-ml): ah. is this the flashattn switch from the rollout?
alyssa (eng-runtime): yes. we flipped heuristic to prefer FlashAttention for all models where head_dim % 8 == 0. but mixtral variants have head_dim=48 and 96 depending on config; flash is rejecting 48 in some kernels. fallback goes to Triton SDPA path which is slower for our batch patterns.
devon (eng-platform): logs? sample error?
alyssa (eng-runtime): paste from worker logs: 
```
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] kernel_select: trying flash_attn
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] flash_attn_init: unsupported head_dim=48 (alignment 16 required)
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] kernel_select: falling back to sdpa_triton (policy=fallback)
[2026-03-15T14:21:03Z] sdpa_triton_exec: kv_cache_hits=0 batch=6 seq=96 latency=12.8ms
```
jonah (eng-runtime): interesting — flash refusing 48 is expected for our optimized 16-wide kernel, but historically we had a custom 8-wide flash kernel for older Mixtral config. Did that get dropped?
maria (perf-sre): profiling snapshot (p95 per-token):
- before change (flash): 3.6ms/token
- after change (fallback sdpa_triton): 8.7ms/token
workload: bursty short responses, mean seq 64, batch size 5.
sam (eng-ml): also note RoPE scaling is slightly different for Mixtral; kv cache layout endianness + mask offset interacts with packing when head_dim not multiple of 16. could be padding path mismatch.
alyssa (eng-runtime): I ran `kernel-prof --model=mixtral-7b --batch=5 --seq=64 --kernels=flash,sdpa_triton,triton_native` — results show flash (if forced via compat shim) still best, but the runtime won't select it due to head_dim check. we used to pad heads to next multiple of 16 in serving compile, but that was reverted for memory reasons.
devon (eng-platform): what's the current kernel selection logic?
alyssa (eng-runtime): simplified: 
```
if head_dim % 16 == 0 and model.supports_flash:
  pick flash
elif head_dim % 8 == 0 and model.supports_sdpa:
  pick sdpa_triton
else:
  pick triton_native
```
that logic is too coarse for Mixtral/LLama families where head_dim=48 (divisible by 16? no, by 8 yes) and our flash variant could work with 8-aligned path but we removed the connector.
jonah (eng-runtime): alternative is to reintroduce an 8-aligned flash shim that pads KV cache on the fly for 8-multiple dims. padding cost might be < regression. we can implement transient pad for first layer and unpad after.
maria (perf-sre): another angle: batching heuristic. with current batcher we coalesce variable-length sequences and pad to max seq which increases effective seq length; flash is more robust to padding because of optimized kernels. sdpa_triton suffers heavily when padded seq increases. if we bias batcher to group similar seq lengths (length-aware binning) p95 improves.
sam (eng-ml): agree. also RoPE scale: our Mixtral-compat preprocessor multiplies cos/sin tables by 1.03 for long-context variants. that affects kv cache reuse because rotated keys don't match cache entries across model variants and we fall back to cold cache often. two issues compounding.
alyssa (eng-runtime): summary of action items I propose: 
1) re-add lightweight flash_8 shim for head_dim % 8 == 0 but % 16 != 0; test on Mixtral-7B and Qwen-7B variants.
2) change batcher to length-aware grouping with a max padding ratio threshold (e.g., pad_ratio <= 1.25) to avoid pathological seq inflation.
3) add RoPE-version tag to cache keys so mismatched RoPE scaling invalidates separately instead of causing silent misses that trigger cold paths.
4) add a microbenchmark in CI that exercises head_dim=48/56/80 cases so kernel selection regressions are caught.

jonah (eng-runtime): I'm +1 on 1 and 3. 2 is lower-risk and can be A/B'd on Canary. I'll prototype flash_8 shim today.
devon (eng-platform): what's the memory/reg cost of dynamic padding in shim? we need numbers to convince infra.
jonah (eng-runtime): rough: for seq=96 and batch=6, extra pad for KV buffers is ~6% memory and adds ~0.5ms to first-token compute but reduces later token latencies by ~2-4ms because we keep fastest kernel. net win for p95. will put numbers in PR.
maria (perf-sre): can we also add a quick metric to console: kernel_selected per model-version and head_dim so support can see when fallbacks occur?
alyssa (eng-runtime): yep that's a small backend metric. I'll open tickets: RB-4212 (flash_8 shim), RB-4213 (length-aware batcher), RB-4214 (kv-rope-tagging), RB-4215 (kernel-selection telemetry + CI microbench).
perf-bot: created ticket RB-4212 by alyssa (eng-runtime).
sam (eng-ml): small note: Qwen variants have head_dim 64 and 128 mostly but qwen-7b with 80 exists in some forks; keep an eye. test matrix should include 48/56/80/96/112 combos.
alyssa (eng-runtime): thanks. I'll run a canary with flash_8 enabled on 5% traffic after jonah's PR. monitoring hook: if p95 improves by <1.2x we auto rollback. 
jonah (eng-runtime): PR up in ~3h. will include microbench results and memory numbers.
alyssa (eng-runtime): awesome, thanks everyone. closing loop here after canary. :thumbsup:
